title: feat(core,react,vue,search,slash,toolbar): editor API, search, slash commands and toolbar enhancements

reviews.body:
## Review: PR #17 — feat(core,react,vue,search,slash,toolbar): editor API, search, slash commands and toolbar enhancements

Thanks for the comprehensive PR — covering 6 roadmap items in one shot is ambitious and the implementation quality is solid across the board. Here are my notes:

### Highlights

1. **Broad roadmap coverage** — Addresses P0 (#5 getSelectedText, #4 onReady, #3 Slash sorting) and P1 (#2 wholeWord, #15 regex, #1 multi-line list toggle) items in a single cohesive PR.
2. **Good test coverage** — Each feature comes with well-structured tests. The toolbar tests especially cover edge cases (mixed list types, toggle-off behavior).
3. **Clean implementation** — `getSelectedText()` is minimal and correct; search options use proper try/catch for invalid regex; slash scoring logic is clear and well-layered.
4. **Framework parity** — `onReady` is implemented consistently across both React and Vue with matching test patterns.

### Issues to address

1. **Merge conflicts** — The PR currently has conflicts that need to be resolved before it can be merged. Likely caused by recent merges on `main` (PR #16 touched `plugin-search/src/index.ts` and `core/src/index.ts`). Please rebase or merge `main` into your branch and resolve the conflicts.

2. **PR scope** — This is a large PR touching 6 features across 15 files. For future contributions, consider splitting into smaller, focused PRs (one per feature). It makes review faster and reduces conflict risk. That said, the code quality here is good enough that this isn't a blocker — just a suggestion for next time.

3. **Minor: `filterSlashCommands` mutates input** — `commands.sort(...)` mutates the original array. Consider using `[...commands].sort(...)` or `commands.toSorted(...)` to avoid surprising callers.

### Verdict

The code itself looks good — once the merge conflicts are resolved, this is ready to go. Please rebase on latest `main`, resolve conflicts, and push. I'll do a final check and merge after that.

Looking forward to the updated version 👍

2. **filterSlashCommands mutation** — 已修复，使用 `[...commands].sort(...)` 避免突变输入数组，详见 `packages/plugin-slash/src/index.ts` 第 89 行

### Code review

Found 5 issues:

1. `findSearchMatches` with `regexp: true` runs the user-supplied pattern straight through `new RegExp(query, flags)` + `doc.matchAll(...)` on the main thread. The try/catch only catches `SyntaxError` at construction; catastrophic-backtracking patterns (`(a+)+$`, `(a|aa)+b`, etc.) hang the renderer at execution. Either run the match in a worker, time-bound the operation, or reject obviously dangerous patterns before constructing.

https://github.com/floatboatai/Nexus-Editor/blob/faddfd3580064f125980e6ab3707f8a17e309857/packages/plugin-search/src/index.ts#L131-L150

2. `wholeWord` wraps the escaped query in `\b…\b`. JavaScript `\b` is ASCII-only — it never matches between two CJK characters — so `wholeWord: true` silently returns zero (or wrong) matches for Chinese/Japanese/Korean queries. In a markdown editor this is a common case. Use a Unicode-aware boundary (lookarounds against `\p{L}` with the `u` flag) or document the ASCII-only limitation.

https://github.com/floatboatai/Nexus-Editor/blob/faddfd3580064f125980e6ab3707f8a17e309857/packages/plugin-search/src/index.ts#L137-L143

3. `plugin-slash` redefines `filterSlashCommands` with a default `limit = 10` and removes the prior `export { filterSlashCommands, getSlashMatch }` re-export from core. Hosts that previously imported `filterSlashCommands` from `@floatboat/nexus-plugin-slash` got every matching command back; they now silently get capped at 10. This is a breaking change for the public API surface with no opt-out and no roadmap/changelog note.

https://github.com/floatboatai/Nexus-Editor/blob/faddfd3580064f125980e6ab3707f8a17e309857/packages/plugin-slash/src/index.ts#L60-L120

4. `getSelectedLines` over-collects when the selection ends exactly at the start of the next line. The loop is `while (pos <= to) { ...; pos = lineEndIdx + 1; }` with `lineStart = doc.lastIndexOf("\n", pos - 1) + 1`. For `doc="Line 1\nLine 2"` and `to=7` (cursor positioned at start of "Line 2", a common CodeMirror line-mode selection), the loop runs a second iteration at `pos=7`, recomputes `lineStart=7`, and pushes `"Line 2"` even though it isn't part of the user's intended selection. None of the new tests exercise a selection ending at a line boundary like this.

https://github.com/floatboatai/Nexus-Editor/blob/faddfd3580064f125980e6ab3707f8a17e309857/packages/plugin-toolbar/src/formatting.ts#L11-L30

5. `toggleOrderedList` and `toggleUnorderedList` collapse the user's selection to a single caret after running. The old single-line code restored the selection at `lineStart + newLine.length`; the new code calls `editor.setSelection(lastNewLineEnd)` only, so a multi-line selection becomes a zero-length cursor at the end of the last toggled line. Chaining toggles (e.g. list → bold) loses the original range, which is exactly the workflow this PR's multi-line capability is supposed to enable. Restore the range to `[firstLineStart, lastNewLineEnd]`.

https://github.com/floatboatai/Nexus-Editor/blob/faddfd3580064f125980e6ab3707f8a17e309857/packages/plugin-toolbar/src/formatting.ts#L80-L95

Lower-confidence flags worth a look (not blocking): the PR bundles ~6 new public capabilities across 6 packages with no `openspec/` change proposal — CLAUDE.md asks AI assistants to consult `openspec/AGENTS.md` for new capabilities, and sibling PRs #13/#14/#15 follow that pattern; PR overlaps with the still-open PR #13 (both add `priority` to `SlashCommandDef` with different scoring semantics — additive bonus here vs separate sort key in #13), so whichever lands second will need conflict resolution; and the `regexp` path silently `return []`s on invalid patterns with no `console.warn` and no README update — the same feedback the maintainer left on PR #9.
